prompt: Override greet() and announce(Object), then add an announce(String) overload, and let the tests show which declared type reaches which method. Complete the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: Overriding and overloading are resolved at different times: the compiler picks WHICH method signature to call from the declared types it can see, and only then does the JVM pick which override of that signature runs, based on the object's real class. That is why the same object answers "Dispatch/String:hi" through a SpeakerDispatch variable and "Dispatch/Object:hi" through a Speaker variable -- the second one never had the String overload in scope. The route helper shows the same trap in miniature: its parameter is declared Object, so the overload is invisible inside it.
hints: Put @Override on greet and on announce(Object); the compiler will then tell you if a signature does not actually match the parent's.
announce(String) must NOT carry @Override -- a different parameter type makes it a new method, not an override.
route needs one line, speaker.announce(value); the point is that value is declared Object there, so only announce(Object) is a candidate.
